problem: Existing outdoor VLN models (Touchdown) predict actions from panorama and instruction features only, so they struggle with complicated urban scenes and ignore fine-grained object details that instructions refer to as landmarks.
motivation: Humans navigate unfamiliar places by using specific objects as reference landmarks, which decomposes a long route into shorter sub-goals. Outdoor VLN agents lack explicit object-level grounding, which limits robustness in unpredictable real-world environments.
key_idea: Add an object-level alignment module (OAlM) that makes the agent attend to object tokens mentioned in the instruction and recognize those landmarks in the views, treating them as sub-goals that split long paths into shorter ones.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablations can be cited. The abstract claims that explicit object-level alignment between instruction landmarks and visual observations makes the agent more object-focused and improves task completion. Landmarks act as sub-goals that decompose long-range navigation.
method: Object-level alignment module (OAlM): guides the agent to focus on object tokens mentioned in the instruction and recognize these landmarks during navigation
Landmark sub-goals: recognized landmarks are treated as sub-goals, decomposing a long path into a series of shorter paths
Integration into a baseline outdoor VLN agent using panorama and instruction features (details not given in the abstract)
